subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept this grouped refresh of privileged GitHub Actions after direct upstream and Codex contract review on a rebased exact head?
rationale: These revisions execute third-party code with secrets, write permissions, publishing credentials, security-upload access, and agent capabilities; repository policy requires explicit human judgment at that boundary.

options.title: Audit, rebase, and merge
options.body: Review the privileged upstream ranges and sibling Codex contract, rebase the bot branch, and merge only after the exact head has acceptable workflow evidence.

options.title: Split privileged updates
options.body: Separate token, Codex, Docker publishing, and CodeQL revisions into smaller PRs if the grouped upstream audit is too broad to approve confidently.

recommendation.title: Audit, rebase, and merge
recommendation.body: Review the privileged upstream ranges and sibling Codex contract, rebase the bot branch, and merge only after the exact head has acceptable workflow evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person to the Docker release, Codex agent, dependency-pin, and broader workflow surfaces affected by the decision.
